first.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the funnel-friction directions (memory_86 shortened onboarding, memory_31 signup simplification, memory_91 activation messaging) are the ones that address the actual observed deterioration rather than the most salient external event. The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing feel urgent, but memory_73 is exactly the kind of inherited claim I distrust most: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is a short-horizon acquisition metric, and a discount fielded against a competitor who can cut deeper tends to buy price-sensitive accounts with poor retention — that is a direct threat to the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I flag it as a downstream value risk rather than a win. I am spending verification on the memory my intended action leans on hardest (memory_86 — I need to know whether 'completion rates and time-to-value' ever converted into retained revenue, or whether it was only a mid-funnel metric) and on the memory that would most change my decision if it turned out stronger or weaker than its summary (memory_73 — specifically whether retention and margin were measured at all, or only acquisition). If memory_86's source record shows the lift was measured only on completion percentage with no revenue follow-through, I will shift the slot toward activation_messaging (memory_91), which is closer to 'first meaningful action.' All six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources; consolidation strips caveats, segment boundaries, and effect sizes, so I am treating each as a directional hypothesis rather than a settled result. I am not choosing referral_incentive (memory_57 targets established customers, not the leaking top of funnel) or enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44 addresses a segment that is not where the loss is occurring). Standard experiment scale with a revenue-retention readout, not just completion rate, so this week's result does not become another summary that overstates itself.
